name: com.adapty.unity-sdk
description: Unity SDK for Adapty in-app purchases, subscriptions, paywalls, and onboarding flows.

_upm.changelog:
Upgrading from 4.0: see [MIGRATION-v4.0-to-v4.1.md](https://github.com/adaptyteam/AdaptySDK-Unity/blob/4.1.0/MIGRATION-v4.0-to-v4.1.md).

### Breaking Changes

- `Adapty.UpdateAttribution(...)` is renamed to `Adapty.UpdateExternalAttribution(...)`, with the `source` parameter renamed to `provider` and typed `AdaptyExternalAttributionProvider` — the shape of the native 4.1 attribution API. The known providers are shared instances (`AdaptyExternalAttributionProvider.Appsflyer`, `.Adjust`, `.AppleAds`, ...); a provider the backend added after this release is constructed from its identifier. No deprecated alias.
- `AdaptyProfile.AppliedAttributionSources` is renamed to `AdaptyProfile.AppliedExternalAttributionProviders`, typed `IReadOnlyList<AdaptyExternalAttributionProvider>` as on the natives. The wire key is unchanged.
- `AdaptyFlow.FlowVersionId` is no longer public. It named the renderer-internal version of the view configuration, which both 4.1 natives keep to themselves; the flow still carries it on the wire. The question that member answered badly — can this flow be rendered? — is now answered by `AdaptyFlow.HasViewConfiguration`, see Added.
- `IAdaptyEventListener` gained `OnReceivePromotedPurchase(AdaptyPromotedProduct)`; implementations must add the method.
- Adapty Attribution is opt-in, and installation details come with it. The 4.1 natives collect installation details only when the configuration asks them to, where the 4.0 natives collected them unconditionally: `IAdaptyEventListener.OnInstallationDetailsSuccess` stops firing and `Adapty.GetCurrentInstallationStatus` stops reporting `Determined` until the app activates with `AdaptyConfiguration.Builder.SetAdaptyAttributionEnabled(true)`. Both platforms behave this way.
- The 4.1 natives read fallback file format 11 and reject the format 10 files v4.0 shipped against, on both platforms: `Adapty.SetFallback` reports `DecodingFailed` (`adapty_code: 2006`) on iOS and `WrongParam` (`adapty_code: 3001`) on Android. Re-download both fallback files from the Adapty Dashboard.

### Added

- `AdaptyConfiguration.Builder.SetAdaptyAttributionEnabled(bool)` — enables the Adapty Attribution service, and with it the installation details.
- `Adapty.MakePromotedPurchase(...)` and `IAdaptyEventListener.OnReceivePromotedPurchase` — App Store promoted in-app purchases (iOS only). The pinned AdaptySDK-iOS 4.1.1 hands the purchase to the wrapper instead of completing it natively, so the listener method is called and `MakePromotedPurchase` is what finishes the purchase. 4.1.0 did not emit the event at all.
- `AdaptyFlow` carries the 4.1 `ui_schema` (custom flow layouts, UIBuilder 5.1) through to the renderer; not public API.
- `AdaptyFlow.HasViewConfiguration` — whether the flow carries a view configuration and can be rendered with `AdaptyUI.CreateFlowView`, answered without calling it and parsing the error. The same flag both natives expose.

### Fixed

- A wrong argument the SDK can catch before sending — a null `placementId`, a null integration `key`, a null `provider`, or attribution data the serializer cannot write — is reported through the completion handler as `WrongParam` (`adapty_code: 3001`), the code the natives answer a wrong argument with. Such a call used to throw at the call site or ride to the native side as a null; nothing reaches the bridge now.
- [Android] An exception thrown by the app's completion handler is caught and logged at the bridge boundary, as it always was on iOS, instead of leaving the SDK through JNI.
- The custom-attribute validation of `AdaptyProfileParameters` throws `ArgumentException` instead of a bare `Exception`, and `AdaptyUICreateFlowViewParameters.SetProductPurchaseParameters` rejects two identifiers sharing one `adapty_product_id` instead of silently collapsing them into a single request entry.
- Custom color and linear gradient assets are now rendered on iOS. An asset built with `AdaptyCustomAsset.Color` or `AdaptyCustomAsset.LinearGradient` and passed through `AdaptyUICreateFlowViewParameters.SetCustomAssets` used to reach the view as a transparent color and an empty gradient; AdaptySDK-iOS 4.1.1 implements the conversion the native side had left as a placeholder, and moving the pin there is the whole of the fix. Custom image and video assets were never affected.

### Native and Protocol

- The native dependencies are pinned to AdaptySDK-iOS 4.1.1, which includes the 4.0.3 hotfix, and on Android to crossplatform 4.1.0 / android-sdk 4.1.0 / android-ui 4.1.0, with the bundled unity-wrapper AAR rebuilt at 4.1.0.
- [Android] `Adapty.RestorePurchases` no longer reports `NoPurchasesToRestore` (1004): the 4.1 native completes with the current profile when there is nothing to restore. iOS never produced the code; the `AdaptyErrorCode` member stays.
- The cross-platform contract is 4.1.1, which is 4.1.0 with its version raised — AdaptySDK-iOS 4.1.1 changed no request, response or type, so the Android crossplatform 4.1.0 implements the same contract. Against 4.0: `update_external_attribution_data`, `make_promoted_purchase`, `did_receive_promoted_purchase`, `adapty_attribution_enabled` and `ui_schema` are new, and the offer identifier of a product request now travels nested as `subscription.offer.offer_identifier` — the flat form is no longer written.
